# Maskera (maskera.dev)

> Swedish-first, local privacy layer in front of every AI model. maskera finds and masks detected Swedish personal data (names, personnummer, addresses, phone numbers, and more) before text reaches an LLM, an AI agent, a log, or analytics. Everything runs on-device (browser via WebGPU/WASM, browser extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox with Safari coming later, local LLM proxy / MCP server via `@maskera/mcp`, or Node); text and restore maps are not sent away for masking. The packages contain no telemetry. The demo counts anonymous, cookieless page views, never your content. The default setup fetches the model weights and WASM runtime once as static assets (both can be self-hosted), never your content. Redactions are reversible via a restore map that stays with the caller.

Three open-source packages (MIT), two detection layers (rules first):

- `@maskera/mcp` (npm): local-first CLI for AI agents with seven subcommands on top of `maskera`:
  1. `npx -y @maskera/mcp wrap -- <cmd>`: one-command launcher that starts an ephemeral local loopback proxy, verifies zero leaks automatically, injects `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `MASKERA_PROXY_URL`, and `MASKERA_MCP_URL` into `<cmd>`, and prints a session receipt when `<cmd>` exits.
  2. `npx -y @maskera/mcp proxy --root <dir>` (plus `--open` or background daemon via `npx -y @maskera/mcp service install`): local HTTP reverse proxy on `127.0.0.1:8787`, for any client that accepts a custom API URL, for Anthropic (`/v1/messages`) and OpenAI (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`), plus a co-hosted warm Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint at `http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp` (supports scoped query parameters `?no_raw_restore=1`, `?read_only=1`, `?approval_mode=browser`) and a live inspector with one-click self-test at `/_maskera`. Automatically redacts outgoing prompts, history and tool results before they leave the device, restores placeholders transparently in JSON, tool arguments and chunk-split SSE streams, and fails closed (`502`) on error.
  3. `npx -y @maskera/mcp --root <dir>`: MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio server (`maskera_list_files`, `maskera_search_files`, `maskera_read_file`, `maskera_write_file`, `maskera_redact`, `maskera_restore`, `maskera_list_sessions`, `maskera_clear_session`, `maskera_status`, plus `maskera_resume` in browser approval mode), bundled MCP `prompts` (`maskera-workflow`, `maskera-redact-file`) and `resources` (`maskera://skills/maskera/SKILL.md`, `maskera://status`), and policy flags `--no-raw-restore`, `--read-only`, `--approval-mode automatic|browser|native`. Keeps raw file contents and restore maps strictly inside local process memory.
  4. `npx -y @maskera/mcp guard`: harness-agnostic hook/pipe guard. Reads plain text, `--file <path>`, or Claude Code/Cursor JSON hook envelopes from stdin; exits `2` with label counts only (never raw PII) when PII is found, or outputs redacted text with `--redact`.
  5. `npx -y @maskera/mcp install [client|all]`: auto-detects or configures `claude-code`, `claude-desktop`, `codex`, `cursor`, `opencode`, or `t3-code` for stdio or Streamable HTTP MCP (supports `--apply`, `--project`, `--with-hook`, `--dry-run`, `--receipt <file.json>`, `--no-verify`, `--no-raw-restore`, `--read-only`, `--approval-mode`), automatically running a synthetic Swedish PII roundtrip + live `/mcp` probe and printing a zero-PII setup receipt (`maskera-setup-receipt/v1`).
  6. `npx -y @maskera/mcp doctor`: verifies Node runtime, workspace roots, a synthetic Swedish PII redact/restore roundtrip, and any running local proxy + live `/mcp` endpoint (supports `--receipt <file.json>` and `--json`).
  7. `npx -y @maskera/mcp service <install|status|uninstall>`: installs, checks, or removes a persistent local `launchd` (macOS) or `systemd --user` (Linux) background proxy service.
- `@maskera/core` (npm): deterministic detectors for structured Swedish PII: personnummer, samordningsnummer, organisationsnummer, phone, email, postnummer, bankgiro, plusgiro, IBAN, cards, IP, URL, plus opt-in context-labeled domestic account and journal identifiers. Format checks and selective checksums reject common look-alikes; personnummer detection deliberately retains real-date values with a mistyped Luhn digit. Zero dependencies, synchronous. Custom patterns join via `regexDetector`.
- `maskera` (npm): everything in core plus the published `maskera-sv-ner` v21, our attested privacy-clean Swedish NER model (KB-BERT fine-tuned and distilled from a 3-seed teacher ensemble to a 43 MB ONNX) that catches free-text names, places, organisations and street addresses, including all-lowercase chat text. Its task-specific training uses 121,200 generated rows and 7,980 disjoint validation rows. On overlap, rules win. The hybrid also enables street address, lägenhetsnummer and context-labeled domestic account/journal identifiers by default; `regnummer` is opt-in. Clinical callers can set `profile: "clinical"` to retain common measurements, doses and care terms.

Quick start (SDK):

```ts
import { createNerRecognizer, redactWithNer } from "maskera"

const recognizer = createNerRecognizer()
const { text, restore } = await redactWithNer(
  "hej jag heter provnamn maskera, personnummer 19900101-2385, och bor i provbyn",
  { recognizer },
)
// "hej jag heter [NAMN_1], personnummer [PERSONNUMMER_1], och bor i [PLATS_1]"
```

Independent Swedish benchmark (the only numbers maskera.dev shows; measured 2026-11-27 on CPU on text neither Maskera nor its developer wrote and that is not in Maskera's training: the SUC 3.0 test split from the National Library of Sweden, SIC2 Swedish blogs from Språkbanken Text, the MultiCoNER v2 Swedish test split (persons only) and the Swedish rows of ai4privacy openpii): Maskera v21 q4 hid 94.6% of names (11,885/12,570), 91.1% of lowercase names, 97.3% of places and 95.3% of street addresses and postcodes. Same cells (names / lowercase names / places / addresses): Microsoft Presidio 2.2.366 with Swedish spaCy sv_core_news_lg 72.3% / 71.4% / 97.1% / 47.0%; swedish-pii 1.2.0 55.3% / 0.3% / 82.7% / 77.3%; OpenAI Privacy Filter q4 ONNX 52.2% / 10.3% / 33.5% / 63.3%. Where Maskera does worse: Maskera puts a detection in 12.3% of entity-free SUC + SIC2 sentences against Presidio's 2.5% (Presidio's spaCy model is trained on SUC 3.0). Personnummer, organisationsnummer, bankgiro and IBAN have no independent Swedish corpus and are not in this comparison; they are covered by format rules with check digits. Machine results: https://github.com/joelhagvall/maskera/blob/main/docs/benchmark-independent-v21.json. Author-written release gates (internal, not shown on the site) are in https://github.com/joelhagvall/maskera/blob/main/docs/BENCHMARKS.md

Deployment boundary: all masking runs locally on the user's device, whether in the open-source npm packages (`maskera`, `@maskera/core`, `@maskera/mcp`), the maskera.dev browser demo, or the Maskera browser extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox (Safari coming later; Free with unlimited rules + 20 AI redactions/month, Pro at SEK 149/user/month incl. VAT with a 7-day free trial and own protected words, or Team at SEK 249/user/month excl. VAT (min. 5 users) with a shared E2EE protected-word list, MDM deployment and annual invoicing). There is no hosted masking API on offer. The customer portal at app.maskera.dev handles accounts, offline extension licences, and billing. Customer text is not processed there.

## When to use Maskera

Reach for Maskera when all of these hold:

- The text is Swedish (or mixed Swedish/English) and may contain personal data: names, personnummer, samordningsnummer, organisationsnummer, addresses, phone numbers, e-mail, postnummer, bankgiro/plusgiro, IBAN, card numbers, IP addresses.
- The text is about to leave a trust boundary: a prompt to an LLM or AI agent, a local file read by an agent, a log line, analytics, a ticket export, a support transcript, a training or evaluation corpus.
- Masking must happen where the text already is (browser, browser extension, local agent proxy/MCP, Node.js) rather than in a third-party API, and it must be reversible for the caller (restore map) but not for the recipient.

Best-fit jobs: enforced pre-LLM redaction for AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Claude Desktop, OpenCode), pre-LLM redaction in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Perplexity, Mistral and internal AI sites, HR/recruiting screening, customer support and complaints, healthcare notes (`profile: "clinical"` keeps doses and measurements), legal and municipal case text, log scrubbing, building de-identified test data from real-looking Swedish text.

Not a fit: non-Swedish text (English names work only incidentally), image/PDF OCR (feed Maskera the extracted text), a hosted "send us your text" API (none exists, by design), or guarantees of zero leaks (see the measured leak counts above and the accuracy page).

## How an agent should call it

Pick the right local integration for the user's environment:

Choose the mode by where the text comes from: **proxy for text typed straight into the chat** (in clients that accept a custom API URL), **MCP for files the agent reads with the Maskera tools**. Before the user sends real personal data, verify the setup with made-up data: send a fictional address and confirm that the local inspector (`http://127.0.0.1:8787/_maskera`) shows a placeholder going upstream.

1. **Local LLM proxy, for clients that accept a custom API URL (recommended when every prompt and tool output must be masked):**
   - Start `npx -y @maskera/mcp proxy` (binds `127.0.0.1:8787`, supports `--port`, `--upstream <url>`, `--audit-log <file.jsonl>`, `--rules-only`, `--profile clinical`, `--custom-term <word>`, `--no-restore`).
   - Configure the agent/SDK base URL:
     - Claude Code / Anthropic SDK: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787`
     - Codex / Cursor / OpenAI SDK: `OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1`
     - Claude Desktop: Help → Troubleshooting → Enable Developer Mode, then Developer → Configure Third-Party Inference…, with base URL `http://127.0.0.1:8787` (no `/v1`), the user's Anthropic API key and the `x-api-key` auth scheme (Anthropic rejects the default Bearer scheme). Step-by-step guide with the exact field names: https://github.com/joelhagvall/maskera/tree/main/packages/mcp#claude-desktop-through-the-proxy
     - Codex signed in with a ChatGPT subscription cannot point at a plain-HTTP proxy; use the MCP stdio server instead.
   - Live local inspector UI (shows masked outbound previews & counts in RAM only): `http://127.0.0.1:8787/_maskera` (JSON counts: `/_maskera/status`).

2. **MCP stdio server (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, T3 Code):**
   - Add to the client's `mcpServers` config:
     ```json
     {
       "mcpServers": {
         "maskera": {
           "command": "npx",
           "args": ["-y", "@maskera/mcp", "--root", "/path/to/workspace"]
         }
       }
     }
     ```
   - Use `maskera_read_file` to read sensitive local files already redacted, `maskera_write_file` to restore placeholders directly to disk without echoing PII into the LLM context, and `maskera_clear_session` when finished.

3. **Hook / shell guard (Claude Code / Cursor hooks or Unix pipes):**
   - Block prompts or hook JSON containing PII: `npx -y @maskera/mcp guard` (exits `2` on PII with counts only, `0` when clean).
   - Redact a stream locally: `cat file.txt | npx -y @maskera/mcp guard --redact`.

4. **Agent skill (workflow rules for any harness):**
   - Install the skill directly from GitHub (`skills/maskera/SKILL.md`): `npx skills add joelhagvall/maskera`.

5. **In application code (browser or Node):**
   - `npm install maskera @huggingface/transformers` (rules + 43 MB Swedish NER model) or `npm install @maskera/core` (rules only, zero dependencies, synchronous). Use `redact(text)` from core, or `createNerRecognizer()` + `redactWithNer(text, { recognizer })` from `maskera`. Keep `map`, send `text`, call `restore(reply)` on the LLM output.

6. **In web AI chats (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Perplexity, Mistral and opt-in internal AI sites):**
   - Install the local Maskera browser extension (Chrome, Edge, Firefox; Safari coming later) from https://maskera.dev/en/services (Swedish: https://maskera.dev/tjanster; Free with unlimited rules + 20 AI redactions/month, Pro at SEK 149/user/month incl. VAT with a 7-day free trial, or Team at SEK 249/user/month excl. VAT (min. 5 users) with a shared E2EE protected-word list and MDM support, via https://app.maskera.dev).

7. **On this site:**
   - Every page has a Markdown rendering. Send `Accept: text/markdown` to any page URL, or fetch the `.md` sibling directly (`https://maskera.dev/index.md`, `https://maskera.dev/en/developers.md`, `https://maskera.dev/en/about.md`). Unknown paths return HTTP 404 with a Markdown (default), JSON (`Accept: application/json` or `/api/*`) or HTML body that lists these entry points. `maskera.dev/api/*` is not an API: it answers 404 in JSON with the same hints.

## Packages and model

- [@maskera/mcp on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@maskera/mcp): local LLM proxy, MCP stdio server, and hook guard for AI agents
- [maskera on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/maskera): rules + Swedish NER model, core re-exported
- [@maskera/core on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@maskera/core): rules only, zero dependencies
- [maskera-sv-ner on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/joelhagvall/maskera-sv-ner): the 43 MB Swedish NER ONNX model, training details
